title: Patch 22 - Table Reading Integration
description: Adds Table Reading as a full AFOQT subject with data table questions testing rapid row/column lookup and numerical comparison.

officialFormat.coordinateSystem: X = columns (top axis), Y = rows (left axis)

mappedGameSubtopics.description: Finding values at specific X,Y coordinates in a data table.
Comparing values across rows or columns to find differences, sums, or patterns.

inferenceNotesForCopilot: Infer difficulty level from the filename: 'table_reading_beginner_part1.json' → difficulty=beginner.
Each JSON file may contain a top-level tableSpec defining the shared data table used by all questions in that file.
Questions use uiSpec type 'data_table' with useTableSpec flag to reference the shared table.
Coordinate system: X = columns (horizontal axis, top headers), Y = rows (vertical axis, left headers).

questionRoutingRules: 2. Each JSON may contain a shared tableSpec at the top level defining the data grid.
3. Questions reference the tableSpec via uiSpec.useTableSpec = true.
4. Aggregate questions into registry by difficulty: questions['table_reading']['basic_table_lookup'][difficulty].
5. For practice tests, select table sets ensuring variety of lookup patterns and coordinate combinations.
uiIntegration: Use data_table uiSpec to render a grid with X (column) headers on top and Y (row) headers on left.
Display a legend above the table explaining: 'X = Columns (Top), Y = Rows (Left)'.
Questions ask for values at specific (X, Y) coordinates or comparisons between cells.
In practice test mode, hide explanations until section is complete.
Emphasize speed: table reading questions are designed for rapid scanning (10.5 sec average).
implementationNotes: Table reading tests cognitive speed and accuracy in finding values in a numeric grid.
Beginner: simple single-cell lookups with small tables (5x5 or similar).
Advanced: multi-step comparisons (e.g., 'difference between X=3,Y=20 and X=5,Y=40').
Expert: larger tables, more complex arithmetic on retrieved values.
Each file may have a shared tableSpec to avoid repetition; questions use uiSpec.useTableSpec = true.
Highlight field in uiSpec (optional) can emphasize specific cells/rows/columns for visual assistance.
Ensure consistent coordinate language: X = columns, Y = rows (never inverted).

validationRules.uiSpecRequired: All table reading questions must have uiSpec with type='data_table'
validationRules.tableSpecFormat: Files may include top-level tableSpec with xHeader, yHeader, and cellValues arrays
validationRules.coordinateConsistency: All questions must use X for columns and Y for rows consistently
validationRules.timingGuidance: 10.5 seconds per question average for full AFOQT simulation (40 questions in 7 minutes)

axisClarity.convention: X = Columns (Top Axis), Y = Rows (Left Axis)
axisClarity.reasoning: Matches standard Cartesian coordinate system where X is horizontal and Y is vertical.
axisClarity.questionFormat: Questions should ask: 'What value is at X = ? and Y = ?' or 'For Y = ?, find X = ?'
axisClarity.uiDisplay: Render legend above table: 'X = Columns (Top) | Y = Rows (Left)' for clarity.
